about: Edges of slice 2 (housing) of /visualizaciones/sistema/. Model (slice 2, housing): annual steps 2026-2050 in deviations from a baseline (INE household projection 2026-2041, completions held at the 2023-2025 average). Rents move with dwellings per household (inverse demand), young adults leave home when rents fall (loop B2), house prices follow rents plus a credit term, and housing credit responds to prices (loop R2). Levers: public completions a year, released land, LTV/LTI caps, rent cap in stressed areas (coverage and % cut), limits on tourist rentals.

parameter.name: respuesta_oferta_tope
parameter.unit: % de caída de la oferta de alquiler de mercado cubierta por cada 1 % de rebaja efectiva del alquiler

items.need: CONTESTED -> debate with >= 3 schools, each with its own source and central value in this SAME unit. How much does the market rental supply in the covered area fall per 1 % of effective rent reduction caused by a rent cap (second-generation controls on new contracts)? Normalise each study: supply change (%) / rent change (%) of covered units. Schools: (a) Catalonia 2020 law (Ley 11/2020): Jofre-Monseny, Martínez-Mazza & Segú (2023, J. Urban Econ., 'Effectiveness and supply effects of high-coverage rent control policies') and/or García-Montalvo & Monràs ('The effect of second generation rent controls: new evidence from Catalonia', 2023); (b) Diamond, McQuade & Qian (2019, AER, San Francisco: landlords treated by rent control reduced rental supply by 15 %); (c) a review: Kholodilin (2024, J. Housing Econ., 'Rent control effects through the lens of empirical research'). Central = your judgement of the most relevant for Spain; low/high = span of the schools. Say in derivation how each normalisation was done and which numbers are approximations. Put in contrary_evidence studies finding no supply effect or effects through quality/maintenance rather than quantity.
items.hints: IZA/NBER/CEPR working-paper versions are easiest to fetch (docs.iza.org, www.nber.org/system/files/working_papers/wNNNNN/wNNNNN.pdf). Barcelona IEB working papers: ieb.ub.edu. AER papers: try the NBER WP version (Diamond, McQuade, Qian NBER w24181).

items.need: Price elasticity of new private housing supply, Spain if possible. Candidates: Caldera & Johansson (2013, J. Housing Econ., 'The price responsiveness of housing supply in OECD countries': long-run estimate for Spain); Banco de España work on housing supply (e.g. Documentos Ocasionales on the housing market 2023-2025); Saiz (2010) only as US contrast. Model use: private completions deviation = elasticity × price deviation two years earlier × baseline private completions (about 80,000 a year).
items.hints: OECD working-paper version: 'The price responsiveness of housing supply in OECD countries', OECD Economics Department WP 837 (www.oecd.org is blocked: try one-search or a mirror such as ideas.repec.org links, or the ECO/WKP pdf on read.oecd-ilibrary.org).

items.need: Distribution of NEW housing mortgage lending in Spain by loan-to-price (LTP/LTV) and loan-to-income (LTI) or debt-service-to-income, latest year (Banco de España Informe de Estabilidad Financiera, spring/autumn 2024-2025, or its data annex). Main parameter: share of new lending VOLUME (or of loans, say which) with LTP > 80 %. extra_parameters: hip_sobre_ltv90 (LTP > 90 %), hip_sobre_ltv70 (LTP > 70 %; if only a 60-80 bucket exists, interpolate and say so), hip_sobre_lti6 (LTI > 6 or the nearest published threshold), hip_sobre_lti45 (LTI > 4.5 or nearest). Accounting, grade A if published by BdE. Low/high = the range over the last 2-3 years published.
items.hints: BdE IEF pdfs: https://www.bde.es/wbe/es/publicaciones/informes-memorias-anuales/informe-estabilidad-financiera/ (look for 'LTP', 'LTV', 'LSTI', 'LTI', 'préstamo-precio'). Also BdE 'Indicadores de la política macroprudencial' (CCA). The ICO guarantee lines for young buyers (from 2023) allow LTP up to 100 %: mention if the IEF says so.

items.need: When tourist rentals are restricted (licences withdrawn, bans), which share of the removed tourist dwellings returns to long-term residential use (rental or owner-occupied) within 1-2 years, vs. staying empty, becoming seasonal/mid-term lets (alquiler de temporada) or continuing illegally? Evidence: Barcelona (licence moratorium, 2028 ban), Valencia, Palma, Lisbon, Amsterdam, New York Local Law 18 (2023: listings fell ~80 %, little change in long-term rental supply per several reports), Los Angeles HSO (Koster, van Ommeren & Volkhausen 2021, J. Urban Econ.). Give central/low/high with derivation; grade B or C, D if only reports/assumption.
items.hints: Koster et al. 2021 Tinbergen Institute DP version (papers.tinbergen.nl). NYC: Inside Airbnb / NYC Comptroller or Office of Special Enforcement reports. Barcelona: Ajuntament reports on 'pisos turístics' converted. Seasonal-lets (temporada) leakage in Spain: say if documented.

items.need: For second-generation rent caps on new contracts (rent at most a reference index), which fraction of the mandated reduction actually shows up in contract rents (non-compliance, side payments, furniture/seasonal lets, reclassification)? Spain first: Catalonia 2020 (Ley 11/2020) with Incasòl deposit data; Catalonia 2024 (Ley 12/2023 zones, from March 2024) if evaluated; compute as measured average rent change of covered contracts / mandated average cut (share of contracts above the index × average gap above it) where the studies give both. Model use: covered rent change = - mandated cut × this fraction.
items.hints: Jofre-Monseny, Martínez-Mazza & Segú (IEB WP 2022/04 or J. Urban Econ. 2023); García-Montalvo & Monràs (UPF/BSE working paper); Generalitat/Incasòl or Agència de l'Habitatge evaluation reports; Kholodilin review.

items.need: Inverse demand / spillover within the rental market: when the market rental supply falls by 1 % (e.g. landlords exit because of a cap), by how much do rents of uncovered units / new searchers rise? Evidence: Diamond, McQuade & Qian (2019): treated supply -15 %, citywide rents +5.1 % (derive the share of the rental stock treated to normalise); Catalonia 2020 spillovers to non-regulated units (García-Montalvo & Monràs; Jofre-Monseny et al.); Autor, Palmer & Pathak (2014, JPE, Cambridge decontrol) as contrast. Give central/low/high in the stated unit with the normalisation.
items.hints: NBER w24181 (Diamond et al.), NBER w18125 (Autor, Palmer, Pathak).

items.need: Share of rental contracts (habitual residence) that are new or renegotiated each year in Spain: new contracts per year (deposits of fianzas, SERPAVI or regional deposit registers; INE/Incasòl) / stock of rented main residences; and the legal duration (Ley 29/1994 LAU art. 9 as amended by RDL 7/2019: 5 years, 7 if the landlord is a company; annual update caps 2023-2024, index from 2025). Model use: rents paid by sitting tenants converge to market rents at this rate. Accounting, grade A if from deposits/law.

items.need: When a borrower-based cap on new mortgages binds, which fraction of the VOLUME of the loans above the cap disappears from new lending? It counts both the mechanical part (a loan at 90 % of price cut to 80 % loses 11 % of its amount) and borrowers who drop out, delay or buy much cheaper; borrowers who add savings or family help to buy the same home lose only the mechanical part. Model use: new lending change = − this fraction × share of new lending volume above the cap. For scale: in Spain 43.8 % of new lending had loan-to-price > 80 % at end-2025 (BdE IEF spring 2026), but the mean loan-to-price is about 78 %, so most loans above 80 % are only slightly above. Evidence: Ireland 2015 mortgage measures (Central Bank of Ireland evaluations; Acharya et al. 2022, 'Real effects of borrower-based macroprudential policy', J. Financial Econ.), UK 2014 LTI flow limit, Netherlands, Israel (Tzur-Ilan), New Zealand LVR; cross-country Alam et al. (2019 IMF iMaPP) and Araujo et al. (2024 meta-analysis of macroprudential policy). extra_parameters: efecto_ltv_meta_precio (house price growth effect of a typical LTV tightening, pp, from a meta-analysis) and efecto_ltv_meta_credito (same for credit growth).
items.hints: IMF is blocked at www.imf.org: try elibrary.imf.org or SSRN/BIS mirrors; Central Bank of Ireland: www.centralbank.ie.
